answer: A sybil-resistant economy should view every newcomer through a prism of accumulated trust instead of raw account counts. Each agent begins its voyage with tiny privileges and a locked stake, and only established peers can attest or vouch, so reputation transfers slowly from real work. Like a lagoon shielded by an expensive reef, the entry cost — stake plus attestation time — makes swarming the network with fake agents unprofitable, while cheaters lose their vouches and sink.
